messages:
maya: Heads-up: Finance noticed a small set of users were billed twice on streaming requests that triggered a mid-stream toolcall after a reconnect+fallback. Filing BILL-600. Anyone seen this pattern?
rob: Seen something similar in staging yesterday. Model=redwood-mini-v2, region=us-east-1, correlated with canary traffic.
maya: Sample trace:
router: session=usr_X route=canary-1
runtime: stream truncated at token=210
client: reconnect
router: fallback->stable-2
runtime: resume, toolcall invoked (no client-provided id)
ledger: provisional +28 tokens acct=acct_12
... later identical provisional committed again
theo: root cause seems to be idempotency key scoped to route/instance. When router switches route the key changes so dedupe misses.
izzy: Quick ideas: 1) runtime-synthesize a canonical id for mid-stream toolcalls based on a prefix-hash (tokenize first N tokens then sha256) and set X-Toolcall-Canonical. Router must forward it unchanged.
rob: 2) ledger-side short TTL tombstone keyed on acct+prefix-hash+tool-name for ~20-30s to catch fast retries across routes. If duplicate, suppress second commit and emit telemetry.
theo: also add a Grafana alert for billing.toolcall_double_finalized_total{model,route} and a trace sample panel. We missed this earlier.
maya: ops-bot: created BILL-600 and assigned to eng-platform (https://internal/p/BILL-600)
ops-bot: <@maya> Ticket BILL-600 created and assigned to eng-platform.
izzy: I'll prototype the runtime canonical header behind a feature flag (cap tokens to 512). Rob, can you own the ledger tombstone?
rob: yes. I'll add the dedupe TTL and an audit log for suppressed duplicates.
maya: Thanks all 44D. We'll canary the runtime change next week and run a backfill to find affected customers.
